findings.title: A repeated opening form
findings.claim: The alif-lām-mīm sequence can function as a recurring threshold sign: its repeated placement makes the rootless letters legible as a formal opening before discourse supplies words.
findings.mechanism: The exact sequence recurs at 2:1, 29:1, 30:1, and 32:1; at 7:1 it is extended by ṣād and followed in the supplied ayah by a book being revealed. This wider pattern returns through the focus's exact letter-name sequence and changes an isolated opaque token into a recognizable entry-form, without supplying a lexical paraphrase.
findings.reader_payoff: A reader can recognize that the opening form recurs and let that formal work matter without waiting for a hidden lexical answer.
findings.containment: The recurrence supports a repeated opening function, not a decoded name or shared hidden gloss; the focus remains the same open alif-lām-mīm form, and other detached-letter openings need not share one interpretation.

epistemic.reason: The supplied target Arabic directly verifies exact recurrence and the 7:1 extension, while interpreting recurrence as a threshold sign is a formal inference and the target morphology is not supplied.
